cards.title: Family Secret: Handling Child Sexual Abuse Allegations
cards.body: When a family member discloses childhood sexual abuse, prioritize making them feel safe to share at their own pace. Assess any ongoing danger the perpetrator poses to younger family members and seek professional support.

cards.title: Empty Nest: Parents Share the Emotional Challenge
cards.body: Parents describe the unexpected grief of their first child leaving for university, despite knowing it's a natural milestone. The experience involves denial, denial, and reconciling your identity beyond active parenting.

cards.title: Second Baby: Relearning Parenting from Scratch
cards.body: New parents of a second child often forget basics like feeding, teething, and sleep routines learned with their first. Grandparents can be invaluable for both practical help and reminding parents of their own carefree childhoods.

cards.title: Why Reasoning With Upset Children Backfires
cards.body: Emotionally reactive children need calm presence more than logical explanations during distress. Stop explaining and focus on regulating your own emotions first.

cards.title: Stop Defending Your Parenting Past, Live Present
cards.body: Constantly justifying past parenting decisions prevents you from enjoying and influencing your child's present life. Let go of the need to prove you were a good parent and focus on being present now.

cards.title: How Father's Depression Biologically Affects Children
cards.body: Research reveals a father's depression impacts his children through biological pathways, not just behavioral modeling. The effects begin earlier and run deeper than previously understood.

cards.title: College Freshmen: Grades Matter, But Friendships Save You
cards.body: Students heading to college should prioritize making at least one genuine friend alongside their academic goals. Strong social connections significantly boost mental health and overall well-being during the transition.

cards.title: Heatwaves May Force Schools to Rethink Calendar
cards.body: Teachers warn that rising temperatures make classroom learning increasingly difficult during traditional hot summer months. Climate change could reshape when school terms run.
